summary: Lookout Mountain north summit near Bellingham, WA: 1930 wooden tower (1931 per one source), Aircraft Warning post 1942-43, now gone; summit holds communication towers.

facts.design: Wooden tower with a 7x7 foot cab and house, framed from single trees by county fire patrol crews, guyed with donated wire rope, one ladder for access
facts.status_note: Tower and house gone per FFLOS and FireLookout.com. SummitPost says the Department of Natural Resources later destroyed it, with no year given. WillhiteWeb says the former lookout sites are now communication tower sites.

access.note: SummitPost says public access is still granted to the two summit areas of the mountain. WillhiteWeb says the former lookout sites are now communication tower sites with very few views.

visit.trail_note: Hike or bike the main road about four miles, avoiding side trails, to a Y intersection; the Whatcom summit and lookout site is 1.5 miles to the right (WillhiteWeb).

events.note: FFLOS and FireLookout.com date the 80-foot wooden tower to 1930; WillhiteWeb dates it to 1931 (see resolved_conflicts).
Activated as an Aircraft Warning Service station on May 21, 1942; the record names the Bellingham Filter Center.

Aircraft Warning station Yoke 0-8 inactivated October 16, 1943. The State of Washington kept the site for a fire detection observation post. A 12-by-20-foot garage was erected with AWS funds (no date given).
Registered May 22, 2012 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register (US 1263, WA 163).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and FireLookout.com give 1930, and the FFLOS photo is captioned June 1930. WillhiteWeb gives 1931 and says a June 1931 date stamp on its photo was written over with 1930. Not resolved; the story gives 1930 and notes the 1931 date.

FFLOS and FireLookout.com give 80 feet. The 1930 association report quoted on Washington Lookouts gives 87 feet in height, 80 feet to the floor and 89 feet overall. The stored 26.5 m matches 87 feet and is kept; the story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: No source read dates the removal, so there is no removed event; SummitPost says the DNR destroyed it without a year. Access raised from unknown to public for the summit areas per SummitPost, not for the tower site itself. The 1930 versus 1931 build year is unresolved and both are in the story. No photos added: the FFLOS photos are credited to the Ron Kemnow collection but no image URL was found.
